style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Utility closet painted drywall. A brushed-steel Zigbee coordinator rail runs horizontally at chest height with 32 shallow child sockets, most empty; one router module seats in the fifth socket from the left, its own 15-socket pigtail branching downward; a coiled USB extension cable lies on a plywood shelf below. A single raking key light from the left throws long cast shadows; bone white, graphite, deep pine green; brushed steel, painted drywall, plywood. Extreme asymmetry with the rail on the left third and empty right negative space. No text, no logos, no people.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI, logos
rationale: This treatment states the firmware child table as a modular mechanical assembly: a rail of 32 slots and a router branching 15 sockets make the arithmetic visible without a literal product shot. It suits the article's structural limit and keeps the home environment grounded.
cue: the real cap is a table of children
subject: A brushed-steel Zigbee coordinator rail with 32 child sockets, most empty, one router module occupying a socket and branching its own 15-socket pigtail.
core_thesis: A Zigbee hub's limit is a firmware child table rather than radio range: the coordinator holds 32 direct children, routers take one slot and add 15, so the cap moves with firmware, not the antenna.
core_conflict: firmware child-table capacity vs radio-range expectation
composition: extreme asymmetry with the rail on the left third and empty right negative space
alt_text: A wall-mounted power strip in a utility corner, one module plugged in, coiled network cables hanging beneath.
caption: Zigbee Hub'S Silent 32-Device Cap: A firmware child table caps the network, not radio range.
title: Zigbee Hub'S Silent 32-Device Cap

review.depicts: A long brushed-metal multi-socket power rail mounted on a wall at left is mostly empty, with a single black module plugged into one socket from which several coiled teal cables hang and loop downward, above a wooden ledge holding a coiled black cable, while the right two-thirds of the frame is bare wall.
review.reason: The image renders the article's mechanism as a metaphor — a fixed row of empty sockets with one occupied module branching its own cables stands in for the 32-child table and a router adding its children — though without a literal Zigbee hub or any visible count of 32 a reader could also misread it as plain electrical hardware.
